name: Finnish TVT versus TVT-O trial
question: How do retropubic TVT and transobturator TVT-O compare for primary surgical treatment of female stress urinary incontinence?

design.blinding: Masking not reported; five-year assessment by an independent physician or research nurse
design.population: Women undergoing primary surgery for stress urinary incontinence at seven Finnish hospitals; prior incontinence surgery, postvoid residual >100 mL, prolapse beyond second degree, and body mass index >35 kg/m² were among the exclusions.
design.description: Multicenter randomized comparative trial; eight TVT-experienced gynecologists each performed at least five TVT-O procedures before enrollment. Sample size assumed 95% TVT success and 70% power to detect a 10% difference in success or complication rates.
design.locator: Laurikainen 2007, Full text, Methods, p 5; Laurikainen 2014, Full text, Methods and Table 1, p 1110

verdictNote: No primary endpoint was designated; two-month stress-test cure was similar, while early complications favored TVT.
takeaway: Among 267 women who underwent the allocated operation, two-month negative cough stress tests followed retropubic TVT in 134/136 (98.5%) and TVT-O in 125/131 (95.4%), without a significant difference. Investigators registered 41 early complications in the 131-woman TVT-O group versus 18 in the 136-woman TVT group.

reports.label: Two-month primary report
reports.dateLocator: PubMed citation: 2007 Jan; day not specified
reports.citation: Laurikainen E, Valpas A, Kivelä A, et al. "Retropubic Compared With Transobturator Tape Placement in Treatment of Urinary Incontinence: A Randomized Controlled Trial." *Obstet Gynecol.* 2007;109(1):4-11. doi:10.1097/01.AOG.0000249607.82768.a1

results.measure: Negative cough stress test at 2 months among operated women analyzed
results.note: No significant between-group difference reported; exact P value, effect estimate, and confidence interval not reported. The paper did not designate a primary endpoint.
results.locator: Full text, Results, p 7; Methods, pp 5-6

results.note: All condition-specific questionnaires improved within both groups (P<0.001 for pre/post comparisons), without a reported between-group difference; no binary subjective cure rate, between-arm effect, confidence interval, or exact P value was reported.
results.locator: Full text, Results and Table 4, pp 7-9

harms.label: Intraoperative and immediate postoperative complications
harms.locator: Full text, Discussion, pp 9-10; Table 2, p 8
harms.note: P<0.001 for Table 2 other complications (15/136 versus 38/131); the discussion gives total registered complications including perforations. One TVT bladder perforation, one TVT retropubic hematoma requiring two-unit transfusion, and one TVT 800-mL bleed were reported. Authors judged the difference not clinically significant.

harms.label: Postoperative opioid analgesia
harms.locator: Full text, Results, p 6; Table 2, p 8
harms.note: P=0.034; postoperative opiate analgesia. Table 2 prints 13% for 16/136 TVT patients, but 16/136 is 11.8%, as printed in the Results text.

harms.label: Postoperative groin pain
harms.locator: Full text, Results, pp 6-7; Table 2, p 8
harms.note: P<0.001; TVT-O pain persisted for 2 weeks in 10 women, 4 weeks in 3, and 2 months in 1.

harms.label: Postvoid residual over 100 mL after 24 hours
harms.locator: Full text, Table 3, p 8; Results, p 7
harms.note: P=0.006; mean time to PVR under 100 mL was 6 versus 9 hours (P=0.033). At 2 months, 8/136 versus 14/131 had PVR over 100 mL. One TVT recipient needed repeat catheterization on day 2; two TVT-O recipients self-catheterized for 1 and 3 weeks.

harms.label: Postoperative urinary tract infection treatment
harms.locator: Full text, Results, p 7; Table 2, p 8
harms.note: Postoperative treatment for urinary tract infection; between-arm P value not reported.

delivery.label: Allocated operations performed
delivery.locator: Full text, Results and Fig. 1, pp 6-7
delivery.note: 267 of 273 randomized women underwent their allocated operation and were analyzed; one TVT-O allocation was converted to TVT for technical reasons and excluded, so 268 underwent surgery.

delivery.label: Hospital stay
delivery.locator: Full text, Results, p 6; Table 2, p 8

delivery.label: Anesthesia, prophylaxis, and immediate voiding protocol
delivery.value: Local 0.25% prilocaine plus adrenaline (75-135 mL) with light IV sedation; single IV cefuroxime 1,500 mg or metronidazole 500 mg at operation start; no indwelling urinary catheter; spontaneous voiding requested within 3 hours
delivery.note: TVT used 70° thigh angle and cystoscopy after each retropubic needle passage; inside-out TVT-O used 90°-110° thigh angle and cystoscopy at operation end.

reports.label: Five-year follow-up
reports.citation: Laurikainen E, Valpas A, Aukee P, et al. "Five-year Results of a Randomized Trial Comparing Retropubic and Transobturator Midurethral Slings for Stress Incontinence." *Eur Urol.* 2014;65(6):1109-1114. doi:10.1016/j.eururo.2014.01.031
reports.followUp: 5 years; 254/268 (94.8%) operated women assessed according to protocol
reports.followUpLocator: Full text, Results and Fig. 1, p 1111

results.measure: Five-year objective success among women assessed: negative cough stress test, negative 24-hour pad test (<8 g), and no SUI retreatment
results.note: The significance threshold was p<0.05; neither five-year primary outcome differed significantly between arms. Exact P value, effect estimate, and confidence interval were not reported.
results.locator: Full text, Methods, Outcomes and Results, pp 1110-1112

results.measure: Five-year expectations completely or partly met, among all operated women
results.note: Complete satisfaction: 115/136 (84.6%) TVT and 113/132 (85.6%) TVT-O. Source prints 94.2% for TVT complete-or-partial satisfaction, but Table 3 counts sum to 128/136 (94.1%). Between-arm difference was not significant; exact P value, effect estimate, and confidence interval were not reported.
results.locator: Full text, Methods, Outcomes, Results and Table 3, pp 1110-1112

results.endpoint: Objective success with missing follow-up counted as failure
results.measure: Five-year objective success among all operated women, missing follow-up counted as failure
results.note: Secondary missing-as-failure analysis; no exact between-arm P value or confidence interval reported.

harms.label: Tape problems requiring a procedure through five years
harms.note: One TVT-O tape extrusion required partial excision and later TVT for recurrent incontinence; one retention case required two midline tape incisions. No tissue reaction, erosion, or tape protrusion was seen among 254 women at the five-year examination. The investigators described overall complication rates as low and similar between groups, with no late-onset tape-material adverse effects reported.

harms.label: De novo urgency incontinence at five years
harms.note: Seven of 254 assessed women; none met urgency-incontinence criteria at two months.

harms.label: Postvoid residual >100 mL at five years
Antibiotic-treated urinary tract infection in preceding two years
harms.note: The paper gives 20.6% for TVT and 22.1% for TVT-O but no arm-specific numerators.

delivery.label: Protocol assessment at five years
delivery.value: 254/268 (94.8%) operated women assessed according to protocol at five years; 131/136 TVT and 123/132 TVT-O
delivery.locator: Full text, Results and Fig. 1, p 1111

delivery.label: Sling technique and concomitant surgery
delivery.locator: Full text, Methods, Study procedures, p 1110
delivery.note: Both were type 1 macroporous monofilament polypropylene, inserted from the vaginal incision under local analgesia with light sedation; cough testing with 300 mL bladder fill guided tape adjustment; cystoscopy in all cases; no concomitant surgery. One woman allocated to TVT-O received TVT because of technical problems.
